title: Unary internal Hom derives to internal RHom from a degree-zero module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $T_M=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(M,-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], assumed additive. Let $S:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] with comparison $\delta:T_M^{\bullet}Q\to QS$ be a right derived functor of termwise internal Hom, for quasi-isomorphisms. Then $S$ is naturally isomorphic to $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(M[0],-)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No local freeness, algebra structure, or adjunction is assumed.

proof.text: Use homComplex_single_natIso to identify the single-source Hom-complex functor H with termwise internal Hom T. This is a natural chain isomorphism, with no exactness assumption.

Take the source-library functorial K-injective resolution I and its quasi-isomorphism eta in the Grothendieck abelian category of sheaves of modules. On the K-injective localizer, quasiIso_homComplex_map with identity source proves that H followed by Q inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Transport through the natural isomorphism to T followed by Q. The K-injective derivability structure then makes delta invertible on I(K).

Specialize derivedInternalHom_comparison at the complex P[0] to obtain Q composed with RHom(Q(P[0]),-) naturally isomorphic to I composed with H composed with Q. Whisker the natural single-source comparison by I and Q.

The natural transformation eta whiskered with Q and S is invertible since eta is a quasi-isomorphism. Compose it with the inverse of delta whiskered with I to obtain Q composed with S isomorphic to I composed with T composed with Q. Compose the comparisons, then descend the natural isomorphism via Localization.liftNatIso for Q. The equality Q(P[0])=singleFunctor(P) is definitional.

proof_origin.place: Sections 0A8X and 08J7, Lemma 0A95; natural single-source comparison and K-injective derivability, followed by localization of the resulting natural isomorphism
